summary: Ag-110m, an activation product with a 249.83 d half-life, passes through intact SiC coatings; AGR-1 compacts released from about 0 % to more than 90 % of it.

nuclides: Pd-105 (not in register);Pd-107 (not in register);Pd-108 (not in register);Pd-110 (not in register)
summary: Palladium has no isotope of radiological consequence but crosses intact SiC and corrodes it, a key contributor to the SiC failures found in AGR-1 particles.
Caesium is effectively retained by intact SiC, so its release measures SiC integrity; Cs-137 is one of the owner's first Phase 2 nuclides.
Strontium passes intact coatings in small amounts and is held in the OPyC and matrix; Sr-90 is one of the owner's first Phase 2 nuclides.
Europium passes intact coatings at levels about ten times those of strontium and is largely held in the OPyC and compact matrix.

summary: Radioiodine is expected to be released like the fission gases through failed coatings; deferred in STRATO because no PyC or SiC iodine diffusivity is registered.
